name: Discover it Miles
balance_transfer_fee: 3% of each transfer during the first 15 months, then 5% on transfers posted at a promotional APR and none at the standard Purchase APR
late_payment_fee: None the first time you pay late, up to $41 after that

welcome_bonus.bonus: Discover Match, which doubles every mile you earn in your first year
welcome_bonus.requirement: automatic on all miles earned from account approval through your first 365 days, with no minimum spend and no cap, paid within two billing periods

verdict.text: A flat 1.5x cash back card in travel language, doubled in year one

earn_rates.category: Travel and every other purchase, unlimited

earn_note: One rate on everything, no categories and no caps. Cashback Match doubles the first 12 months, so year one effectively earns 3x. Worth knowing what miles means here: there are no airline partners, so 1.5x at a penny each is 1.5% back in travel wrapping.

redemption_options.method: Partner gift cards, which carry at least 5% added value
Statement credit against a travel purchase
Deposit to a bank account, in any amount

points.note: The thing that genuinely sets this apart: cash is worth exactly as much as travel. Discover says so twice on its own page, that miles "keep the same value" however you redeem, and 100 miles is $1 either way. Most travel cards quietly cut cash redemptions to half a cent, which is how a 1.5x card turns into 0.75% back if you ever stop booking flights. That does not happen here, so there is no penalty for taking the money. Travel redemptions work as a statement credit against a purchase you already made, covering airfare, hotels, rideshares, gas and restaurants, rather than a booking portal you have to shop inside. Gift cards became available to Miles cardholders with the move to Capital One and carry the same guaranteed 5% minimum added value as the rest of the lineup, which makes them the best standing option, though Discover's own Miles page still lists only the cash and travel routes. Discover also prints its own hedge that redemption rates may vary and are subject to change.

transfer_partners.highlight: No airline or hotel transfer partners. Despite the name, Discover Miles are a fixed-value currency, not a transferable one.

protection_note: This is the row that should give a travel shopper pause. A card sold on travel carries no trip cancellation, no trip interruption, no baggage delay, no travel accident insurance and no rental car coverage. Discover cut its protections in February 2018, price protection followed that October, and the current cardmember agreement contains no benefit terms at all. Competing no-fee travel cards usually keep at least rental coverage or trip delay, so if a cancelled flight or a lost bag is the risk you want covered, this card does not do it and no amount of miles earning changes that.
rental_note: No rental car coverage of any kind. Booking a car with this card leaves the collision waiver decision entirely to your own auto policy or the rental counter, which is a real gap on a card marketed for travel.

services.name: $0 fraud liability
services.detail: You are never held responsible for unauthorized purchases. No enrollment needed.

services.name: Free FICO score
services.detail: Your FICO score from TransUnion on your statement and in the app, with the factors moving it. Discover offers this to non-cardholders too, so it is not really exclusive.

services.name: Social Security number alerts
services.detail: Daily dark web scans for your SSN plus new-account alerts on your credit report. Requires enrollment, and only the primary cardmember can sign up.

services.name: Freeze It
services.detail: Freeze the account from the app or website to block new purchases and cash advances if you misplace the card.

services.name: 24/7 US-based customer service
services.detail: Live agents at any hour, without a menu tree to fight through first.

additional_cards.title: Additional cards

benefits.text: Their spending earns miles into your account
Counts toward Discover Match in year one
Any travel or rental car coverage

additional_cards.note: Free to add, and worth doing in year one, since an authorized user's spending gets matched alongside yours.

timeline.text: When your own account moves to Capital One, three earning routes switch on that Discover never had: 5% on hotels, rental cars, vacation rentals and activities booked through Capital One Travel, 5% on tickets and events through Capital One Entertainment, and Capital One Offers for online shopping. Migration runs in waves into 2027, so these are not live for most cardholders yet, and Discover's own product pages do not list them.

Capital One begins moving Discover card accounts onto its own platform on July 27, in waves running through 2027. Account numbers, existing earn rates, rewards balances, APRs and the Discover network branding all stay put, and migrated accounts also pick up the new Capital One earning routes. Redemption changes though: the gift card minimum rises from $5 to $25, and Pay with Rewards through Apple Pay goes away.
Capital One completes its acquisition of Discover Financial Services. Discover Bank later merges into Capital One, N.A., though the cards keep Discover branding and terms.
Price protection is discontinued, following the larger round of cuts earlier in the year.

Discover drops purchase protection, extended warranty, return guarantee, auto rental collision coverage and travel accident insurance across its consumer cards. This is why the protections section below is empty.
